title: How a P-Trap Works: The Mechanics of Sewer Gas Control
description: The P-trap is a critical component of sink drainage designed to prevent harmful sewer gases from entering a building. Located directly beneath the sink tailpiece, its curved shape holds a small volume of standing water after every discharge. This standing water creates a continuous liquid seal, blocking the gas pathway between the drainage pipe and the room. When wastewater drains from the sink, water momentum carries waste past the dip while leaving fresh water behind to replenish the seal. Proper downstream venting prevents pressure fluctuations from siphoning this protective water barrier away.

How a P-Trap Works: The Mechanics of Sewer Gas Control

The P-trap is a critical component of sink drainage designed to prevent harmful sewer gases from entering a building. Located directly beneath the sink tailpiece, its curved shape holds a small volume of standing water after every discharge. This standing water creates a continuous liquid seal, blocking the gas pathway between the drainage pipe and the room. When wastewater drains from the sink, water momentum carries waste past the dip while leaving fresh water behind to replenish the seal. Proper downstream venting prevents pressure fluctuations from siphoning this protective water barrier away.
